Windows therefore promotes every touch to emulated mouse messages (menus work 'by touch' exactly like that) and the game only ever receives MouseItems -> MouseMapper active -> InputMode stays Mouse and TouchMapper::render is never called. (2) The initial mode is Mouse because the fake AnalyticsInfo DeviceFamily is 'Windows.Desktop' (win32_host.c fake_analytics_device_family), which is also what stock Windows 10 tablets report, so stock tablets also start in Mouse mode and rely on rule (1) of the game (touch pointer events) to switch. facts.summary: Verified call plan to deliver touch to the game (option A). For every touch contact keep a host map Windows pointerId -> slot (lowest free 0..11, same policy as 0x627af0). Down: make_MultitouchItem(a=1,b=1,x,y,slot). Move: (0,0,x,y,slot) (only while in contact). Up/cancel: (1,0,x,y,slot) then free the slot. x,y = client pixels scaled to the swap-chain buffer exactly like the mouse path (arm32_scale_pointer_to_buffer), clamped to int16. Enqueue with arm32_enqueue_input(input_handler, item) (EnqueueInput 0x587294, &slot semantics). Do NOT also send MouseItems for the same contact.

facts.summary: Switching back to Mouse needs no host work: any MouseItem (action 0 move, 1/2/3 buttons, 4 wheel - i.e. the existing queue_mouse_event path for REAL mouse/pen messages) makes MouseMapper::tick return 1 and, if no touch is down/just released in the same tick (Touch is later in the mapper vector and wins ties), the mode becomes Mouse and ClientInstance::onInputModeChanged re-grabs the mouse when the scene wants it. Keyboard events never switch modes (KeyboardMapper mode = 0). Host rules: (a) drop touch/pen-promoted mouse messages so that a finger does not flip the game back to Mouse a frame after the touch ended (WM_POINTER handling returning 0 does that; fallback = GetMessageExtraInfo signature filter); (b) do not synthesise mouse items on a timer; (c) host mouse-capture helpers (center_mouse_cursor/SetCursorPos) must not emit relative MouseItems unless a real mouse moved.
evidence: MouseMapper::tick returns 1 on any queued mouse event; Keyboard/Gaze/DeviceButton/BehaviorAction getInputMode = 0 (keyboard_gamepad_motion_mappers)

port_instructions: ROOT CAUSE: the host only injects MouseItems (type 0). The game switches its InputMode in InputHandler::tick (0x5abb44) from the mappers that report device activity; only MultitouchItems (type 1, factory 0x62a174, Multitouch::feed 0x5b00ec) make TouchMapper (0xdbba20) report and select InputMode::Touch (2); the on-screen touch controls are drawn by TouchMapper::vf6 (0x5b242c) and only while the current mode is Touch (renderInputMapperControls 0x3783ac). There is no game setting and no presence query to fix.

1) Add to win32_host_arm32.h (via gen_constants / facts json): ARM_INPUT_MAKE_MULTITOUCH_EVENT 0x0062a174 with expected bytes 2de9f04b0df1180b81461020 (first 12 bytes), ARM_INPUT_MULTITOUCH_ITEM_TYPE 1, ARM_INPUT_MULTITOUCH_ITEM_SIZE 0x10, ARM_INPUT_MULTITOUCH_VTABLE 0x0136ddf8 (data cell, expected file value 0x00a23bcd).

2) Add static BOOL queue_touch_event(int buttonId, int data, int x, int y, int slot) under #ifdef WIN32CRAFT_ARM32 next to queue_mouse_event: reuse arm32_input_target() and arm32_scale_pointer_to_buffer(); clamp to int16; build locals int a,b; short sx,sy; BYTE pid; call the factory as plain AAPCS with 6 args (r0=&item, r1=&a, r2=&b, r3=&sx, stack: &sy, &pid); require *(BYTE*)(item+4)==1; arm32_enqueue_input(). Log the first 12 events like queue_mouse_event does.

3) window_proc (ARM only): handle WM_POINTERDOWN/UPDATE/UP/CAPTURECHANGED for PT_TOUCH as described in plan_touch_events (slot table of 12 entries, lowest-free allocation, release all slots on WM_KILLFOCUS/WM_CAPTURECHANGED, return 0 for touch, DefWindowProcW for other pointer types). Use GetProcAddress for GetPointerType/GetPointerInfo so the DLL still loads on systems without them. Fallback for missing pointer API: RegisterTouchWindow(hwnd,0)+WM_TOUCH (GetTouchInputInfo: dwID, x/y in 1/100 px screen coords, TOUCHEVENTF_DOWN 0x2/MOVE 0x1/UP 0x4) or the extra-info filter below.

4) In WM_MOUSEMOVE/WM_LBUTTON*/WM_RBUTTON*/WM_MBUTTON*/WM_MOUSEWHEEL (ARM only): `if ((GetMessageExtraInfo() & 0xFFFFFF00) == 0xFF515700) return 0;` (MI_WP_SIGNATURE: touch/pen generated) so promoted mouse never reaches the game; keep real mouse messages unchanged (they switch back to Mouse mode automatically).

5) Keep DeviceFamily 'Windows.Desktop' (a 'Windows.Mobile' family changes unrelated game behaviour). Optionally hook the slot-154 cell (plan_initial_mode_patch) so touch-only machines start in Touch mode.

6) Do not make the host depend on the game having entered Touch mode: touch contacts must be delivered regardless of the current mode (the first contact is what switches it). Do not send MouseItems for touch contacts.

7) Add the diagnostics of plan_diagnostics (mapper list, mode transitions, touch event log) so one device log answers: was a TouchMapper created, did touches arrive as pointers, did the mode flip to Touch, did something flip it back to Mouse.

8) Risks to test on device: (a) first tap while in the main menu: the menu is rebuilt for $touch; (b) on-screen text entry without a hardware keyboard still needs the Windows touch keyboard (MinecraftKeyboardManager::show uses the fake InputPane) - separate topic; (c) mouse-capture helpers must not fight the touch drag; (d) 12 simultaneous contacts maximum (slots 0..11).

Exact content of ClientState beyond the first dword (current InputMode at node+0xc) and the meaning of InputHandler+0x100/+0x104 objects: not needed by the host.

TouchMapper::tick was not decoded in full (control hit-testing, UI pointer event generation); the touch controls' on-screen rectangles come from 'binding.area.*' RectangleAreas computed natively (ClientBindingFactory::vf4 0x3763c4, lambdas returning members at +0x2c...); a wrong HUD size/safe-zone would be a separate issue after the controls appear.

Per-mode option persistence key format "%s_%s" (<key>_<ModeName>) is inferred from InputModeBoolOption::vf2; the exact options.txt names for the touch toggles were not checked against a real options.txt written by the game on a device.

Windows RT 8.1: GetPointerType/GetPointerInfo/WM_POINTER availability for plain Win32 windows on RT 8.1 follows MSDN (Windows 8+) but was not run; the WM_TOUCH/extra-info fallbacks exist for that reason.
Pen contacts are ignored by the stock handlers (device type 1); the plan lets pen fall through to the mouse path, which is a deliberate simplification.

Option B (invoking the stored CoreWindow pointer delegates with fake WinRT objects) was only specified, not verified: the delegate Invoke signature (vtable[3](self, sender, args)) is the usual C++/CX TypedEventHandler layout but the HIDController lambda thunk was not disassembled.
